summary: A 1975 survey of the state of New-Protocol Telnet servers, listing which sites had which features working. It is a status snapshot. It updates RFC 701, RFC 702 and RFC 669; see also RFC 703.

eli5.summary: A teacher checking again which students finished their work. This is the February 1975 check on the new Telnet servers.

questions: new protocol telnet servers on socket 27
subtitle: The February 1975 progress check on new-protocol Telnet servers, with progress even slower than before.

tldr.problem: The ARPANET community was still waiting for server hosts to move to the new Telnet protocol.
tldr.mechanism: D. W. Dodds re-ran the survey from the new-protocol user Telnet at BBNA on 20 February 1975 and listed what changed since RFC 669, with an updated summary and table.
tldr.outcome: 18 of 36 server hosts (50%) had a new-protocol implementation, yet the author calls progress even slower than before. It updates RFC 669 and is updated by RFC 703.

today: RFC 679 is a snapshot from early 1975. It updates RFC 669 and was updated by RFC 703. The RFC index lists its status as Unknown.

sections.title: What Changed Since the Last Survey
sections.content: The report comes two and a half months after the previous one, and the author finds it depressing that progress toward an all-new-protocol network has been even slower than before. Changes (host numbers in octal) include: SRI-ARC (2) and OFFICE-1 (53) added logger socket 27 but with old-protocol servers; LL-67 (12) now has a new-protocol server on socket 1; SDC-CC (110) was removed until it starts operating; CASE-10 (15) left the network; BBN-TENEX is now host 361; and ANL (Argonne, 67) came on the net with old and new servers on sockets 1 and 27.
sections.eli5: The note lists which computers joined, left or changed since the last check, and the author sounds a bit gloomy about how slow it is.

sections.title: The Summary Counts
sections.content:
Of 36 server hosts, 17 (47%) had no new-protocol server, 1 (3%) was of unknown status and 18 (50%) had a new-protocol implementation. Of those 18, 10 (28%) used the new protocol on socket 27 with the old one on socket 1, 6 (16%) used it on both socket 1 and socket 27, and 2 (6%) used it on socket 1 only.

The data come from a survey program plus a few manual checks, as seen from BBNA on 20 February 1975.
sections.eli5: Out of 36 computers, 18 had the new tool and 17 did not.

sections.title: The Tabulation and Options
sections.content:
The table lists each server by host number and name, with entries for socket 1 and socket 27 (Old, New, X for no server, ? for not ascertained) and the options implemented. I# means the option is implemented incoming to the user (server says WILL #) and O# outgoing from the user (server says DO #).

Options implemented by anyone are 0 Transmit-Binary, 1 Echo, 3 Suppress-Go-Ahead and 6 Timing-Mark. SU-AI is marked as returning improper responses to some option requests.
sections.eli5: The table is a checklist with a row per computer and columns for which new features it can do.

references.text: Dodds, D. W., "November, 1974, Survey of New-Protocol TELNET Servers", RFC 669, December 1974.
